key_insight: A stationary 1/f spectrum emerges when a system is described by two separated frequency scales (flowing from f_low to f_high) and no other constant parameter besides the mean amplitude, making 1/f noise a generic asymptotic outcome.
engineering_relevance: This provides a simple, system-agnostic criterion for identifying or designing components and models that may exhibit 1/f-type fluctuations, including turbulence-like intermittent regimes.
method: Analytical study of the ordinary diffusion equation
Combined the derived spectrum with known scaling results from fluid turbulence
Used the result to infer a necessary and sufficient condition for stationary 1/f noise
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical derivation and comparison with established turbulence scaling; no new experimental or numerical dataset is mentioned.
watch_item: The condition is stated for stationary noise over a clear frequency band, so real systems with extra parameters, finite-size effects, or nonstationarity may deviate from ideal 1/f behavior.
paper_title: Condition for $1/f$ noise to occur along with an example for a diffusion equation
